biography.plain_text: Dave Paton is an Australian marine biologist who founded Blue Planet Marine in 2002. The consultancy provides environmental research, monitoring and training across Australasian and Antarctic waters. His doctoral work at Southern Cross University examined the conservation and recovery of eastern Australia's humpback whales, earning him a PhD in 2016.
biography.html: Dave Paton is an Australian marine biologist who founded Blue Planet Marine in 2002. The consultancy provides environmental research, monitoring and training across Australasian and Antarctic waters. His doctoral work at Southern Cross University examined the conservation and recovery of eastern Australia's humpback whales, earning him a PhD in 2016.

confidence.reason: Official company material establishes founding, date, services and waters served; the university's thesis record establishes the degree, subject and 2016 award. Australian background agrees with the source record and independently anchored Australian research identity.

long_biography.plain_text:
As director of the Southern Cross Centre for Whale Research, Dave Paton linked photographic identification with genetic studies of migrating humpbacks. Student volunteers collected pieces of skin shed by the animals for DNA analysis. Surveyors on land directed field teams towards whale pods so that photographs and genetic samples could be collected together.

Paton was the principal photographer at Byron Bay for a collaborative study comparing sightings along Australia's east coast. Matching patterns on the undersides of humpback tails enabled the researchers to recognise individual animals. By combining photographs from Byron Bay, Hervey Bay and Ballina, the team estimated the migrating population's size.
long_biography.html:
As director of the Southern Cross Centre for Whale Research, Dave Paton linked photographic identification with genetic studies of migrating humpbacks. Student volunteers collected pieces of skin shed by the animals for DNA analysis. Surveyors on land directed field teams towards whale pods so that photographs and genetic samples could be collected together.

Paton was the principal photographer at Byron Bay for a collaborative study comparing sightings along Australia's east coast. Matching patterns on the undersides of humpback tails enabled the researchers to recognise individual animals. By combining photographs from Byron Bay, Hervey Bay and Ballina, the team estimated the migrating population's size.
